question: Should the exact-head scoped cache and SQLite predicates be accepted as preserving the existing cross-process subagent session-state contract?
rationale: Tests and supplied runtime proof are strong, but the change alters persistence-read boundaries for session lifecycle data, where the repository requires owner judgment before accepting non-obvious state risk.

options.title: Accept scoped semantics
options.body: Confirm the cache, fallback, ordering, and in-memory precedence contract, then merge after required checks pass.

options.title: Request broader lifecycle proof
options.body: Require an additional multi-process run covering concurrent persistence and reads across the 500 ms cache window before merging.

options.title: Pause the optimization
options.body: Keep broad hydration until maintainers choose a different canonical strategy for cross-process registry snapshots.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped semantics
recommendation.body: Confirm the cache, fallback, ordering, and in-memory precedence contract, then merge after required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing candidate for the affected agent registry and session-state boundary.
